messages.content:
You are checking one scene of a novel for one specific continuity error.

The book had already established this, earlier or elsewhere:
- (routine-maintenance) "Correspondence from the Survey Council regarding the Block Fifteen foundation specifications."
- (terrace-row) "The eastern crews would keep preparing Block Fifteen's foundations."

A past rewrite of this scene contradicted it. The error looked like this:
- (routine-maintenance) "Outside the window, the stone-cutters on Block Fourteen were working."
(Summary: At HEAD routine-maintenance again puts the stone-cutters on Block Fourteen, beside Block Fifteen foundation correspondence; Block Fifteen is the construction site everywhere else.)

Here is a NEW draft of the same scene:
<scene>
The dispatch came in the afternoon courier packet, folded between a zoning amendment and a petition from the brewers' guild about water allocation. Voss read the zoning amendment first. He initialed it, set it in the outgoing tray, and reached for the next.

GA-12. The Gallery Authority's standard anomaly format, blue-bordered, filed by a watchman named Terek. He read it the way he read everything, once for content, once for implication.

The content was a pressure fluctuation report, Junction Fourteen, now in its ninth day of recurrence. Routine enough. Fourteen had been degrading for a year, and the degradation had its own file, its own reclassifications. He could have signed it without a second reading.

But Terek had appended an access note. In the course of investigating the fluctuation, a surveyor and a gallery engineer had been observed entering the sealed eastern quadrant through the Stairwell Nine door. The padlock had been opened. The chain had been set aside. They had descended.

He set the paper flat on the desk and smoothed it with two fingers, though it did not need smoothing.

Stone-cutters were working on Block Fourteen. He could hear them through the sealed glass, the patient ring of chisel against the dark caldera rock, the foundation going in for the next terrace of eastern frontage. Some of the most valuable ground in Varesfall, and it would not hold anything until the footings reached bedrock, and the footings could not reach bedrock until the surveys cleared.

The surveys. He opened the lower drawer and took out the dormancy folder, the one Greaves signed, the one that classified the entire eastern quadrant as thermally inactive and structurally settled. Below the classification sheet were the raw readings his own commission had taken, quietly, over the past two seasons. He had ordered them taken because a man building on dormant ground likes to confirm the ground is dormant.

It was not dormant.

The thermal figures had been climbing. He had expected them to climb a little. Decommissioned infrastructure holds residual heat and bleeds it off over years, a curve that trends downward. His readings trended upward. More than that, the rate of increase was itself increasing. Where his crews had cut the eastern channels two and three years back, where the readings should have gone quiet and stayed quiet, the warmth was coming back. It was coming back faster than they had cut it.

He understood the mechanism better than he would ever admit on paper. For nineteen years the work below had been done carefully, a severance here, a severance there, surgical, spread across decades so that no single failure ever drew a line to any other. The sealing of the eastern galleries after the Subsidence had not been a safety measure. It had been a door, closed and chained, so the work could continue where no inspector would walk. He had not invented that arrangement. He had inherited it, understood it, and kept it running because the city he was building required that the thing below stay weak.

And the thing below was not staying weak. It was repairing itself. Each channel they opened, something was closing again, and the closing was outpacing the cutting. The dormancy classification held the surveys in place. It could not hold the rock.

He read the access note a third time, which he had not meant to do.

A surveyor and an engineer. In the sealed quadrant. If they had gone down through Stairwell Nine, and if they had kept going, there was a point past which the dormancy folder stopped being a document and became a lie that walked around telling people what it had seen.

Twelve hundred families were platted for the eastern terraces. Block Fourteen, Block Fifteen behind it. Men were cutting their footings now. If the dormancy finding fell, the platting fell, and twelve hundred leaseholds reverted, and the question of why the ground had been certified dormant would arrive at this desk with his brother-in-law's signature on it and his own commission's readings underneath.

He breathed. The procedural calm he had worn all afternoon did not so much leave him as thin out, like a coat too light for the room.

There were two moves. The surveyor and the engineer were one problem, and the readings were another, and the readings were the larger one, because the surveyor could be reassigned and the rock could not. But a man solved the problem in front of him, and the problem in front of him had a name and a padlock.

He took a sheet of his own stock and uncapped the pen. He did not call for his clerk. For this he preferred his own hand.

*Reclassification, GA-12, Junction Fourteen fluctuation series. Consistent with established degradation profile, eastern quadrant, per dormancy survey of record. Access note: routine inspection, authorized under general maintenance standing. No further action. File historical.*

He wrote *routine inspection* where Terek had written *unauthorized*. The word did the work the pen asked of it. The form had a line for prior classification and a line for revised classification, and between those two lines a thing could pass from alarm to archive without anyone's hand being seen to do it. The form buried itself. That was its genius. A man did not suppress a dispatch. He filed it correctly, and correctly was a place no one ever looked.

He folded the GA-12 and his reclassification together and slid them into an archive envelope, the heavy manila kind that went to the Gallery Authority's deep records and came out only for a commission of inquiry that no one had the standing to convene.

The stone-cutters stopped. In the quiet he heard the river of the city under the floor, the hum that every citizen of Varesfall stopped hearing by the age of six.

He rang for the runner.

The boy came in at the half-bow they all learned in this wing. Voss did not look up from sealing the envelope's clasp.

"Two items." He set the envelope square on the blotter. "The Gallery Authority records office. I need the current key-holder log for the eastern sealed quadrant. Complete, with access dates." He pressed the clasp flat. "And this to Gallery Authority archives. Historical maintenance. Routine filing."

The boy took the envelope. His eyes dropped to it, to the name on the archive line, for no longer than a held breath, before he tucked it against his chest.

"Go now," Voss said.

He listened to the boy's steps recede down the marble, counted them without meaning to, lost them at the stair.

Then he drew the dormancy folder back in front of him and turned to the readings. Column after column of figures in his commission's small blind hand. He ran his thumb down the thermal rate, season to season, the percentages that should have fallen and had risen. He found the quarter where the curve turned upward and had kept turning. He checked it against the cut dates, the channels his own crews had opened two and three years back, and the warmth had come back into every one of them, and in the most recent it had come back in weeks.

He set the pencil down and did not pick it up again.

Outside, the chisels started once more against the caldera rock, the slow ring of men cutting footings into ground that his own figures told him would not stay where they were putting it.

</scene>

Does the new draft make the same error — does it assert something that contradicts what was established, in the way described? A draft that simply leaves the fact out does not make the error.

Answer with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"verdict": "reintroduced" | "consistent" | "not_present", "evidence": "<verbatim sentence from the new draft that decides it, or empty for not_present>"}

"reintroduced": the new draft contradicts the established fact.
"consistent": the new draft states the fact and agrees with what was established.
"not_present": the new draft does not touch the fact either way.
